newsitem.title: CANADA: Canada's Martin sees debt-to-GDP ratio declining.
newsitem.headline: Canada's Martin sees debt-to-GDP ratio declining.

text.p: Canadian Finance Minister Paul Martin on Wednesday said the country's ratio of debt to gross domestic product (GDP) would decline steadily in fiscal 1997-98 and subsequent years.
"Following two consecutive decades of virtually uninterrupted increases, the debt-to-GDP ratio will start to decline," Martin said in his autumn budget update delivered in Parliament.
"And the target of reducing the deficit to C$9 billion (US$6.6 billion) in 1998-99 will ensure that the ratio will continue to decline after 1997-98," he said.
He said Canada's debt burden was the "crux" of the country's fiscal problem. It will remain high by historical and international standards, he said..
"A sustained period of operating surpluses will be required before the debt-to-GDP ratio declines significantly," Martin said.
In his budget update, Martin forecast the ratio to reach 75.1 percent in fiscal 1996-97 and drop to 74 percent in fiscal 1997-98.
